standard_prerequisites.name: The inverse system of quotients by the powers of an ideal is pro-isomorphic to the inverse system of Koszul complexes on the powers of a generating set
standard_prerequisites.use: Replaces the quotient system by the Koszul system, which is a complex of finite free modules sitting in finitely many degrees.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Koszul complex on the n-th powers of a set of r generators sits in degrees from -r to 0, so source and target of the comparison have cohomology concentrated in a fixed bounded range
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the pro-isomorphism criterion applicable by bounding the degrees in which the systems live.

standard_prerequisites.name: An isomorphism of pro-objects of a derived category is detected on cohomology in each degree, and one may replace a bounded complex by a bounded above complex of finite free modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement to a pro-isomorphism of modules in each degree for a convenient representative of the complex.

core_obligations: Write the ideal as generated by finitely many elements and replace the system of quotients by the Koszul complex on the n-th powers of those generators, using the pro-isomorphism between the two systems (proof lines 29025-29031).

Observe that the Koszul complex sits in the finitely many degrees from minus the number of generators to zero, so that source and target of the comparison have cohomology confined to a fixed range; apply the pro-isomorphism criterion to reduce to a pro-isomorphism of modules in each single degree (proof lines 29031-29045).

Choose a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded above complex of finite free modules onto the given complex and rewrite the comparison maps as the maps induced by the reductions of that complex (proof lines 29045-29051).

Invoke the Artin-Rees consequence, which identifies both sides of the comparison in each degree with the pro-system given by the quotients of the cohomology by the powers of the ideal, and conclude (proof lines 29051-29056).
proof_roadmap: Replace the quotient system by the Koszul system in the derived tensor product (proof lines 29025-29031).
Bound the degrees and reduce to a pro-isomorphism on cohomology in each degree (proof lines 29031-29045).
Replace the complex by a bounded above complex of finite free modules and conclude with the Artin-Rees consequence (proof lines 29045-29056).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a Noetherian ring, an ideal and a bounded complex of finite modules, the comparison between the derived tensor product with the quotients by the powers of the ideal and the plain quotients of the complex is an isomorphism of pro-objects (statement lines 29014-29023). The proof is a chain of three reductions: the quotient systems are replaced by Koszul systems, whose finite degree range makes the pro-isomorphism criterion applicable on cohomology in each degree, and the complex is then replaced by a bounded above complex of finite free modules so that the Artin-Rees consequence identifies both pro-systems with the quotients of the cohomology (proof lines 29025-29056). The degree bookkeeping and the last identification are what make the argument work. The counted span refers three times, twice to results of this chapter and once to a pro-isomorphism criterion of another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
